title: Finite locally constant subsystems of a torsion local system
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $G$ be an abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Assume its underlying set sheaf is a local system [def-per-ind-finite-etale-local-system] and every element of each geometric stalk [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is killed by some positive integer. Then the finite locally constant subgroup sheaves of $G$, ordered by inclusion, form a small filtered poset whose union is $G$. Finite locally constant means etale locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf of a finite abelian group [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Both the colimit of their underlying set sheaves and their colimit as abelian sheaves identify with $G$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 7.2.6, p. 303: the torsion local system is written as the filtered union of its finite local subsystems.

proof.text: The set-local-system calculus writes the underlying set sheaf of $G$ as a filtered union of finite local-system subsheaves $E$, where finite local system means represented by a finite etale $X$-scheme. By the finite-etale representability theorem, every such $E$ is a finite locally constant set sheaf. Thus a section of $G$ is etale locally in one such $E$; no global factorization of an arbitrary section is asserted.

source.place: Expose XVII, Definition 7.2.1 and Proposition 7.2.3, p. 301; finite-subsystem reduction in Lemma 7.2.6, p. 302. Finite-etale representability is the cited theorem.

proof.text: Apply the finite torsion generated-subgroup lemma to each inclusion $E\hookrightarrow G$ from Step 1. Its hypotheses are precisely that $X$ is Noetherian, $G$ is an ind-finite etale set local system with torsion geometric stalks, and $E$ is finite locally constant. It supplies a finite locally constant abelian subgroup $H\hookrightarrow G$ containing $E$. Consequently the finite subgroup sheaves cover $G$ locally on sections.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 7.2.6, p. 303, finite local subgroup systems in the torsion case.

proof.text: The zero subgroup is finite locally constant, so the poset is nonempty. Given finite locally constant abelian subgroup sheaves $H_1,H_2$, the finite-local-abelian comparison makes their underlying set sheaves finite locally constant. By finite-etale representability they are finite local-system subsheaves of $|G|$. The filtered finite-subobject assertion of the set-local-system calculus gives a finite local-system subsheaf $E$ containing both. Representability makes $E$ finite locally constant, and the generated-subgroup lemma gives a finite locally constant abelian subgroup $H$ containing $E$, hence containing $H_1$ and $H_2$. This proves directedness without asserting that finite stalks alone imply local constancy. Smallness follows by choosing a small skeleton of the etale site in the fixed universe: a subgroup subsheaf is determined by a subset of $G(U)$ for each object $U$, and these choices form a set. Replacing the site by that skeleton does not change its sheaves or inclusions.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 7.2.6, p. 303, ordered family of finite local subgroup systems.

proof.text: Steps 1 and 2 say that the sheaf union is $G$: any section $s$ on $U$ has an etale cover on each member of which $s$ lies in a finite subgroup sheaf. For a compatible family of maps from these subgroup sheaves to a set sheaf $F$, define the image of $s$ locally using these maps. On overlaps, directedness puts any two chosen subgroups in one subgroup, so compatibility makes the local images equal. The sheaf axiom glues them uniquely, independently of all choices, and this construction commutes with restrictions. This is exactly the set-sheaf colimit universal property. For abelian $F$ and homomorphisms in the family, refine a cover to represent two sections and put their subgroup sheaves in a common upper bound; the local image of their sum is the sum of the local images. The glued map is therefore additive, and the same uniqueness proves the abelian-sheaf colimit assertion. The empty scheme and the zero sheaf are covered by the zero subgroup case.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 7.2.6, p. 303, final filtered-union assertion.

lean.statement: theorem torsion_local_system_finite_subsystem (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (G : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (hG : IsIndFiniteEtaleSheaf ((sheafCompose X.smallEtaleTopology (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).obj G)) (htorsion : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X) (g : (pointedEtaleStalk G t : AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})), ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ n • g = 0) : ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : PartialOrder I) (S : I ↪o Subobject G) (ι : S.monotone.functor ⋙ Subobject.underlying ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj G), IsFiltered I ∧ (∀ i : I, ι.app i = (S i).arrow) ∧ (∀ H : Subobject G, (∃ (𝒰 : Cover.{u} etalePrecoverage X), ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (A : AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (_ : Finite A), Nonempty ((H : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).over (𝒰.etalePrecoverageToEtale j) ≅ (constantSheaf (X.smallEtaleTopology.over (𝒰.etalePrecoverageToEtale j)) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj A)) ↔ ∃ i : I, S i = H) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk G ι)) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit ((sheafCompose X.smallEtaleTopology (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).mapCocone (Cocone.mk G ι)))
